facts.statement: The genus Pistosaurus was first described by Karl von Zittel in 1887.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Zittel, 1887

facts.statement: The genus Pistosaurus was originally named by Meyer in 1839.
facts.quote: authority: Meyer, 1839

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Pistosaurus is Pistosaurus longaevus.
facts.quote: type_species: Pistosaurus longaevus

facts.statement: The type species Pistosaurus longaevus was named by Meyer in 1839.
facts.quote: type_species_authority: Meyer, 1839

facts.statement: Fossils of Pistosaurus have been found in France and Germany and date to the Middle Triassic.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in France and Germany, and date to the Middle Triassic.

facts.statement: Pistosaurus is distinguished by a long, slender snout, splint-like nasals excluded from the external naris, and a premaxilla extending to the frontals.
facts.quote: the long, slender snout; the possession of splint-like nasals that are excluded from the external naris; and the posterior extension of the premaxilla to the frontals.

facts.statement: Both Pistosaurus and Plesiosauria belong to the Triassic-originating clade Pistosauroidea.
facts.quote: Both Pistosaurus and Plesiosauria belong to the clade Pistosauroidea, which originates from the Triassic.

facts.statement: Pistosaurus had a stiff vertebral column like a plesiosaur, implying it used paddle-like flippers to propel itself through water.
facts.quote: However, the vertebral column was stiff, like that of a plesiosaur, implying that the animal used its paddle-like flippers to propel itself through the water, as the plesiosaurs probably did.

facts.statement: The head of Pistosaurus resembled a plesiosaur but had a primitive nothosaur palate and numerous sharp teeth for eating fish.
facts.quote: The head also resembled that of a plesiosaur, but with the primitive palate of a nothosaur, and numerous, sharp teeth ideal for catching and eating fish.

facts.statement: The description of Pistosaurus is based on a specimen examined by paleontologist Sues in 1987.
facts.quote: The description below is based on the specimen examined by paleontologist Sues in 1987.

facts.statement: Analysis of muscle grooves suggests Pistosaurus engaged in slight subaquatic flying with most propulsion occurring on the hindlimbs.
facts.quote: Together with the muscle grooves, they determined that a slight subaquatic flying starts with Pistosaurus, and most of the propulsion occurs on the hindlimbs.

facts.statement: Bone processes in Pistosaurus aimed to increase body density to offset buoyancy for an aquatic or semi-aquatic lifestyle.
facts.quote: The ultimate goal of these processes is to increase density for different parts of the body to offset the buoyancy, in order to live in an aquatic/semi-aquatic environment.

facts.statement: Bone histology by Krahl showed Pistosaurus humeri medullary regions were filled with calcified cartilage incorporated into endoseal bone.
facts.quote: Bone histology of Pistosaurus studied by paleontologist Krahl showed that the medullary region of the humeri was filled, and it contained calcified cartilage incorporated into endoseal bone.

facts.statement: Krahl attributed the small medullary region in Pistosaurus to suppressed perimedullary resorption activity associated with osteosclerosis.
facts.quote: According to Krahl, the small medullary region of is the result from a suppressed perimedullary resorption activity, which is associated with osteosclerosis.

facts.statement: Pistosaurus moved limbs simultaneously underwater, contrasting with terrestrial reptiles that move limbs alternatively.
facts.quote: This feature contrasts to the terrestrial reptiles who use their right and left limbs for locomotion alternatively.

facts.statement: While Nothosaurus remains are found across Europe, Pistosaurus skulls were only found in the Germanic Basin in the Upper Muschelkalk.
facts.quote: Although Nothosaurus, which is closely related to Pistosaurus, is known from several remains found across Europe, the latter's skull was only found in the Germanic Basin in Upper Muschelkalk.

facts.statement: Initially, Plesiosauria were suggested to be related to Pistosauroidea, a group belonging to Triassic Eusauropterygia.
facts.quote: Initially, Plesiosauria were suggested related to Pistosauroidea, which belongs to Eusauropterygia from Triassic.

facts.statement: A discovery by Sander indicates Augustasaurus is closely related to Pistosaurus, despite differences in the axial skeleton.
facts.quote: A later discovery of a new Pistosauridea from middle triassic of Nevada by paleontologist Sander indicates that Augustasaurus is closely related to Pistosaurus, while there are several difference including axial skeleton.

facts.statement: It is unlikely Pistosaurus was a direct ancestor of plesiosaurs, though its mixed features suggest a close relationship.
facts.quote: Although it is unlikely that Pistosaurus was a direct ancestor of the plesiosaurs, the mixture of features suggests that it was closely related to that group.

facts.statement: H. V. Meyer discovered the first Pistosaurus skulls.
facts.quote: The early discovery of Pistosaurus skull was made by H. V. Meyer.

facts.statement: Geissler was the first to describe the Pistosaurus skeletons, followed by Strunz who proposed a new hypothesis.
facts.quote: Geissler first described the skeletons and then Strunz developed a new hypothesis based on that.

facts.statement: A Pistosaurus skeleton was originally kept in Strunz's collection at the Senckenberg Museum in Frankfurt.
facts.quote: This skeleton was originally preserved at Strunz's collection in Senckenberg Museum at Frankfurt.

facts.statement: The genus Pistosaurus was named by Meyer in 1839.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Meyer, 1839

facts.statement: The genus Pistosaurus includes the species Pistosaurus longaevus and possibly Pistosaurus grandaevus.
facts.quote: subdivision: Pistosaurus longaevus Pistosaurus grandaevus?

facts.statement: Pistosaurus lived during the Middle Triassic, about 240 million years ago, in what is now France and Germany.
facts.quote: Pistosaurus es un género representado por una única especie de pistosaurio que vivió en el Triásico medio, hace 240 millones de años, en lo que hoy es Europa, en las actuales Francia y Alemania.

facts.statement: Pistosaurus was about 3 meters long and had a rigid spine, suggesting it swam by moving its limbs rather than undulating its body.
facts.quote: Este animal de 3 metros de longitud presentaba una columna vertebral rígida, de modo que debió de nadar impulsándose con las extremidades y no ondulando el cuerpo como una serpiente.

facts.statement: Pistosaurus had a head similar to plesiosaurs but a notosaur-like palate and numerous sharp teeth suited for catching fish.
facts.quote: La cabeza era muy similar a la de los plesiosaurios, pero poseía un paladar como el de los notosaurios, y numerosos dientes afilados, ideales para capturar y devorar peces.

facts.statement: Pistosaurus measured about 3 meters (10 feet) in length and had a body shape similar to the aquatic Triassic reptiles known as notosaurs.
facts.quote: El Pistosaurus medía unos 3 metros (10 pies) de largo y su forma corporal se asemejaba a la de los notosaurios, reptiles acuáticos que prosperaron durante el Triásico.

facts.statement: Pistosaurus had a rigid spine like plesiosaurs, implying it used oar-like flippers for propulsion in water.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la columna vertebral era rígida, como la de un plesiosaurio, lo que implica que el animal usaba sus aletas, similares a remos, para impulsarse en el agua, como probablemente hacían los plesiosaurios.

facts.statement: Pistosaurus possessed a thickened crest crossing the anterior part of the coracoid, a shared trait with plesiosaurs.
facts.quote: Esta característica es una sinapomorfia presente en plesiosaurios: una cresta engrosada que atraviesa transversalmente la porción anterior de la coracoides para conectar la región glenoidea.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the thickened coracoid crest in Pistosaurus is related to the compressive force generated by limb movement.
facts.quote: Se sugiere que esta característica está relacionada con la fuerza de compresión ejercida por el movimiento de las extremidades en Pistosaurus.

facts.statement: The largest recorded humerus of Pistosaurus, analyzed by ARI Cruickshank, is 245 mm long and 45 mm wide at the mid-shaft.
facts.quote: Un ejemplar del húmero izquierdo de Pistosaurus, analizado por el paleontólogo ARI Cruickshank, es uno de los más grandes registrados: 245 mm de largo y 45 mm de ancho en la diáfisis media.

facts.statement: The femur of Pistosaurus is longer than its humerus.
facts.quote: El fémur del Pistosaurus es más largo que su húmero.

facts.statement: Bone histology of Pistosaurus longaevus studied by Krahl showed that the humerus medullary region was filled with calcified cartilage incorporated into the endochondral bone.
facts.quote: La histología ósea de Pistosaurus longaevus, estudiada por el paleontólogo Krahl, mostró que la región medular de los húmeros estaba llena y contenía cartílago calcificado incorporado al hueso endoselado.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Diedrich determined that a slight form of underwater flight begins with Pistosaurus, based on examination of the pectoral and pelvic girdles and muscle grooves.
facts.quote: El paleontólogo Diedrich examinó otras partes de la cintura pectoral y pélvica de Pistosaurus. Junto con los surcos musculares, determinó que un ligero vuelo subacuático comienza con Pistosaurus.

facts.statement: Most propulsion in Pistosaurus was generated by its hind limbs.
facts.quote: La mayor parte de la propulsión se produce en las extremidades posteriores.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Pistosauroidea were direct ancestors of plesiosaurs, as a new Augustasaurus specimen challenges this theory.
facts.quote: Although the Pistosauroidea has long been considered as structural antecedents of plesiosaurs, a new specimen of Augustasaurus, discovered by paleontologist Sandra from Nevada, had raised to debunk this theory.

facts.statement: Based on new evidence, Pistosauroidea was reclassified as a paraphyletic group relative to Plesiosauria rather than their stem ancestors.
facts.quote: Therefore, Pistosauroidea was removed from stem group Plesiosauria and became a paraphyletic group to Plesiosauria.

facts.statement: Surmik suggested that avascular necrosis in Pistosaurus forelimbs indicates it lived in aquatic or semi-aquatic environments.
facts.quote: According to Surmik, the presence of decompression syndrome-related avascular necrosis in Pistosaurus forelimbs suggested that it lived in aquatic or semi-aquatic environments.

facts.statement: Surmik proposed that Pistosaurus may have inhabited cold open marine waters, surviving due to its effective metabolism.
facts.quote: He also stated the possibility of it being distributed in open marine cold waters, and their effective metabolism is one of the reasons why this animal can survive into the open sea.

facts.statement: There are 7 recorded fossil occurrences of the genus Pistosaurus.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 7
